mod.overview: Red Moon RPG is a total-conversion multiplayer action role-playing mod for Starsiege Tribes developed by Deus_ex_Machina, Chee2, Jobo, and the Red Moon team. It transforms base Tribes team combat into an open-world fantasy adventure set in persistent mission worlds like RMR, where players select classes, fight wandering monster factions, complete NPC quests, level up to 999, and amass Gil. The mod replaces Tribes jetpacks, hitscan chainguns, and energy weapons with stamina-driven foot movement, weight-based encumbrance tiers, line-of-sight melee swings, physical arrow projectiles, and an extensive school of elemental and status magic. Gameplay centers on safe town hubs like Rin Vale featuring interactive merchant bots, blacksmith forging stations, banking vaults, and player-bred Chocobo mounts, contrasting with dangerous wilderness dungeons and lawless free-for-all player-versus-player zones.
notes: Classes, Archetypes, and Level Progression: Characters choose from four broad groups including Priest (Cleric, Druid), Rogue (Thief, Bard), Warrior (Fighter, Paladin, Ranger), and Wizard (Mage, Summoner). As players level up toward the level 999 maximum, class titles progress across five tiers at levels 1, 50, 100, 300, and 999 (for example, Fighter advances to Berzerker, Knight, Guardian, and Godly Guardian). Characters manage seven core attributes (Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, Stamina, and Luck) that directly govern physical damage, defense ratings, spell failure rates, and carrying capacity.

Movement Physics, Encumbrance, and Armor Tiers: Player movement speeds are tied to carried weight versus max capacity (calculated from Strength multiplied by 1.25). Being overweight drops the player through seven progressively sluggish armor speed tiers (stepping down every 5 units of excess weight), whereas staying lightweight and wearing agility items can upgrade players into accelerated sprint, gliding, and functional jetpack tiers. Wearing body robes swaps the player model into robed variants, and equipped accessories dynamically alter character meshes.

Melee Combat, Projectile Bows, and Class Commands: Melee weapons like swords, axes, maces, and daggers perform active line-of-sight raycasts to strike players, monsters, and player-erected Magic Walls. Bows consume arrows from inventory or equipped Quivers and launch physical projectile entities with gravity drop. Specific classes possess unique active skills invoked through chat, such as #bash for Fighters and Paladins to double their Strength damage on the next melee swing, #hide for Rogues to turn invisible, and #track for Rangers to calculate the exact direction and distance to other players.

Spellcasting and Magic Systems: Magic includes elemental offensive spells (Fire, Ice, Wind, Earth), curative heals, status clouds, and utility magic like Fire Wall, Hold, Confusion, Manipulation (possessing control of other players or bots), and town teleports. Spells are cast using the #cast command, consuming mana and triggering channeling delays and recovery cooldowns. Casters with 15 or less Wisdom suffer a 20 percent failure chance (dropping to 0 percent at Wisdom 51 or above), and being afflicted with the Mute status silences all speech and prevents spell initiation.

Chocobo Mounts, Stables, and Breeding: RMRPG incorporates a full Chocobo mount and breeding system with rideable vehicle entities and custom animations. Chocobos span four rarity tiers: common Yellow (25000 Gil), uncommon Red, Blue, and Green (100000 Gil), rare Black and White (400000 and 600000 Gil), and legendary Gold (unbuyable, bred exclusively from Black and White pairs as the fastest speed 55 mount). Players can own up to six Chocobos, feed them specialized foods to boost individual stats (Meats for Strength, Fruits for Intelligence, Vitamins for Constitution, Seeds for Wisdom, Candies for Dexterity), and breed them with other players via stables and the #breed command.

Economy, Equipment Slots, and Blacksmith Forging: The economy runs on Gil (COINS), which can be earned from combat, deposited into town bank vaults, spent at merchant shops, or traded via #trade and #dropgil. Characters can equip up to 10 rings, 40 gems, and 1 each of body armor, boots, back gear, shields, talismans, helmets, gauntlets, leggings, and floating orbs. A dedicated blacksmithing system lets players forge customized weapons, armor, suits, shields, and jewelry from gathered raw materials like Metal, Wood, Rock, and Fabric using the #smith command.

Survival, Wilderness Camping, and Status Afflictions: Players must sustain Stamina using provisions like bread, rations, steak, and Uber Burgers. Carrying a Tent allows players to set up an outdoor shelter using the #camp command, creating a private camp zone where they and invited party members can use #sleep to rapidly regenerate health, mana, and stamina while saving their logout spawn coordinates. Hostile hazards include drowning in Water zones without a protective Orb, and four status debuffs: Poison, Blind, Mute, and stone Petrify (which freezes the player until cured by a teammate using a Soft elixir).

Zones, PvP Rules, and Death Penalties: Maps are divided into Protected safe zones, Dungeons, Water zones, and FreeForAll areas. Outside FreeForAll zones, illegally killing an innocent player marks the attacker as a PKer for 15 minutes, allowing anyone to legally hunt them. Low-level players (level 10 and under) enjoy death protection without experience loss, but players above level 10 drop a percentage of their gained experience and leave behind a lootbag containing all carried Gil and mounted equipment (or all carried items if their Luck stat is negative); self-killing via Ctrl-K inflicts an extra 500 EXP per level penalty.

Interactive Town NPCs and Modern HUD Compatibility: Settlements like Rin Vale feature interactive TownBots (merchants, bankers, trainers, blacksmiths, quest givers) that converse with players and react to keywords like buy, yes, no, deposit, and withdraw. Mayor Alice supplies starter equipment and introductory questlines involving sewer runs and undead graveyard investigations. The mod supports both classic Tribes menu interfaces and the modern KronosHUD repack, which adds health bars, party frames, target nameplates, and graphical shop overlays.
